title: Decider working-set reduction (PROP-040 Phase 2). Empirical cost data shows decider is the #1 cost agent at ~$30/day, dominated by 17M cache_read tokens per 22-min run. PROP-040 Phase 1 split decider-curmudgeon.md; Phase 2 needs to attack the per-turn working-set (open-issues + closed-issues + curmudgeon reviews) the way PROP-021 attacks curmudgeon's dispatcher state.
context:
PROP-101 cost instrumentation (shipped 2026-06-14) produced its first empirical decider runs overnight. Two runs of cost-history.jsonl show the following per-run profile:

  Model: claude-sonnet-4-6 (CLAUDE.md says Opus — STALE; runtime is empirically Sonnet)
  Duration: 1316s and 1360s (22-min runs)
  LLM turns: 136 and 158 assistant messages
  Tokens: 16M and 19M cache_read; 433K and 476K cache_write_1h; 119K and 132K output
  Cost per run: $9.17 and $10.49 (mean $9.83)
  Cost composition: cache_read 52%, cache_write_1h 28%, output 19%, input 0% (fully cached)
  Cadence: 3 runs/day → ~$29.50/day → ~$10.8K/year

Decider is the #1 cost agent in the pipeline (curmudgeon #2 at ~$26/day, analyst #3 at ~$22/day). The cost is dominated by VOLUME PROCESSED PER TURN, not by per-token price — at 158 LLM turns × ~108K cache_read per turn, each turn re-reads ~108K tokens of context. The structural lever isn't 'switch models' (decider is already on Sonnet — itself a hidden ~$18/day savings vs Opus) or 'fewer runs' (cadence is already throttled to 3 slots/day post-PEAK-SHIFT). The lever is SHRINK THE PER-TURN WORKING SET.

PROP-040 was the first attempt at this — it split decider-curmudgeon.md into a separate reference file loaded only when Priority 4 (expansion integration) fires. That landed and is implemented. The working-set still includes:

  - decider.md (1334 lines, currently)
  - All reference files loaded conditionally per the dispatcher (intake / curmudgeon / patches / reporting)
  - SCIENTIFIC-CONTEXT.md + DATA-SCHEMAS.md + BUILD-AND-CHANGE.md
  - open-issues.json (current size ~169KB)
  - closed-issues.json (current size 1.4MB+)
  - curmudgeon-pending-digest.json
  - human-notes.json
  - priority-queue.json
  - changes/

The big-volume reads are the JSON state files, not the prompt files. PROP-021 (curmudgeon dispatcher precompute) discovered this pattern for curmudgeon: '46K tokens of state-file input vs 16KB of prompt prose'. Decider likely has a similar 80/20 — most of its 17M cache_read tokens are state files re-read each turn, not prompt tokens.

The parallel-PROP-021 fix for decider: precompute the slice of state the decider's dispatcher needs into a slim artifact (recent closed-issues, open-issues triage queue, pending digest items, attention-inbox snapshot) that the LLM reads ONCE per run, eliminating the per-turn re-read of the full files. Same precompute-and-slim pattern PROP-020 + PROP-021 established for integrity and curmudgeon.
task: Design PROP-040 Phase 2: per-turn working-set reduction for decider. Same precompute-and-slim pattern as PROP-021 used for curmudgeon. Author as PROP-NNN with phased rollout (Phase 0 measurement → Phase 1 precompute ship → Phase 2 prompt slim conditional on measured ≥40% input-token reduction).
investigation_questions: Q1 — Measurement first. Before designing the fix, instrument decider to log per-step input-token counts. The 17M cache_read/run number is aggregate; we need to know which step (intake, M1/M2/M3, BAU 3b triage, queue pop, integration, end-of-run sweeps) consumes how much. Recommend a single bash invocation at end of each step that captures `${ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_TOKENS:-?}` or similar from the last LLM call into a per-step log. Without this, the precompute target is guesswork.

Q2 — Working-set inventory. Walk decider.md + reference files + bash blocks that read state-file JSON. Map every `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(...))` call to: which step it fires in, file size, whether the result is used once (read-and-discard) or referenced repeatedly across turns. Identify the high-volume files (likely closed-issues.json at 1.4MB+) and which steps actually need full content vs a precomputed summary.

Q3 — Precompute candidate design. For each high-volume file, propose a slim artifact a precompute script can emit. Examples: closed-issues-recent-90d.json (drop pre-cutoff entries — decider rarely re-opens older closures), curmudgeon-pending-digest already exists but its size? open-issues-triage-slice.json with only fields the dispatcher needs (id, status, age, severity, assigned_to — drop full body), attention-inbox-counts.json (just summary numbers + first-5 IDs). Mirror PROP-021 approach: precompute artifact in monitor/integrity/decider-dispatcher-state.json (Phase 1) → curmudgeon-style prompt slim that reads ONLY the artifact (Phase 2 gated on measurement).

Q4 — Who runs the precompute? PROP-021 chose hybrid: integrity runs it daily + curmudgeon-side bash refresh on every run. For decider the same shape is defensible but the freshness window matters more — open-issues.json changes every decider run, so a 24h stale artifact misses today's items. Recommend: integrity daily refresh + decider-side bash refresh in clone-setup. Same precedent.

Q5 — Cache-write-1h cost. 28% of decider's cost is cache_write_1h ($2.85/run). This fires whenever the cached context is invalidated and re-primed. If the precompute artifact CHANGES every run (because state changes every run), the cache write may not benefit. Need to think about: which parts of the working set are stable across runs (could be cached for 1h) vs which churn every run (would invalidate cache anyway). The precompute's WIN is reducing the size of the churn-every-run slice, not the stable-cacheable slice.

Q6 — Other-side: decider's job is high-stakes triage that downstream agents depend on. Cutting working-set reduces what the LLM 'sees' per decision. Are there decisions decider currently makes correctly because it has full closed-issues visibility that it would get wrong with just recent-90d? Real risk; need empirical proof the slim works before committing. Phase 1 measurement should include a shadow-mode test where the precompute is produced but decider keeps reading the full files (measure 'would the slim have changed any decision?').

Q7 — Ordering vs PROP-021. PROP-021 Phase 2 (curmudgeon prompt slim) hasn't shipped yet — only Phase 1 (script + integrity check). The natural sequence: ship PROP-021 Phase 2 first (proves the pattern at curmudgeon's smaller scale ~17M curmudgeon cache_read), measure the savings empirically, then apply the lessons to decider's larger surface. Alternatively: design PROP-040 Phase 2 NOW so the operator can ship them in parallel and compound the savings sooner. Recommend the latter — the pattern is well-validated by PROP-020 already; the design work doesn't need to wait for PROP-021's prompt-slim measurement.

Q8 — Estimated savings. If PROP-040 Phase 2 hits PROP-021's claimed 40-70% input-token reduction, decider's cache_read drops from 17M to ~7-10M per run. At Sonnet's $0.30/M cache_read, that's $2-3 saved per run × 3 runs/day = $6-9/day = $2.2-3.3K/year. Plus modest cache_write_1h reduction (~$0.50-1/run = $1.5-3/day). Total ~$8-12/day = $3-4K/year. Worth doing but not transformative on its own; the bigger win is establishing the pattern on a high-volume agent so the same precompute infrastructure can be reused for other heavy-state agents.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 instrumentation design — concrete bash for per-step token capture; (2) Q2 working-set inventory with file-by-file analysis; (3) Q3 precompute candidate list with prioritized recommendation; (4) Q4 who-runs-it (mirroring PROP-021); (5) Q5 cache-write impact analysis; (6) Q6 shadow-mode validation design; (7) Q7 ordering recommendation (parallel with PROP-021 Phase 2 vs sequential); (8) Q8 estimated savings with explicit assumptions. Phased rollout: Phase 0 measurement + shadow → Phase 1 precompute ship → Phase 2 prompt slim conditional on ≥40% input-token reduction. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: Honor the other-side: decider's high-stakes triage role means cutting working-set carries real downstream-mistake risk. Phase 0 shadow validation (precompute produced + decider keeps reading full files + post-hoc compare 'would the slim have given the same decision?') is REQUIRED before any prompt slim ships. Same discipline as PROP-021 Phase 1's measurement-only stance.
Do NOT propose changing decider's model (Sonnet vs Opus) in this PROP. That's a separate operator decision with different trade-offs (judgment quality vs cost) and tinker should not bundle them.
Do NOT propose changing decider's cadence. PROP-031's BAU triage discipline depends on the current 3-slot off-peak structure.

Mirror PROP-020 / PROP-021 conventions exactly: precompute artifact in monitor/integrity/, script in monitor/scripts/, integrity §7N check, file-ownership classification (likely 'git' like drift-audit.json).

Code-sharing: PROP-021's compute-curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.js exists. If the precompute logic for decider's slim artifact is structurally similar (read JSON files, slice by date/status, emit JSON), recommend extraction into a shared monitor/scripts/dispatcher-state-precompute-lib.js that both call. Don't duplicate.

related_prop_lineage: PROP-040 — decider context-load extraction, Phase 1 implemented. Phase 2 is this directive's deliverable.

PROP-021 — curmudgeon dispatcher optimization, Phase 1 implemented (script + integrity check), Phase 2 pending measurement. Same precompute-and-slim pattern; this directive mirrors its design discipline.
PROP-020 — drift-audit precompute pattern; the original PROP that established the precompute-and-hand-off pattern this directive scales to decider's state files.
PROP-101 — cost instrumentation that produced the empirical data motivating this directive. The 17M cache_read figure is the headline.

not_in_scope: Decider model change (Sonnet vs Opus). Separate trade-off.
Decider cadence change. PROP-031 BAU discipline depends on current cadence.
Cross-agent precompute generalization. Stay focused on decider's working set; if the shared lib emerges (Q5 code-sharing), document it but don't make it the headline.

Direct integration / measurement of downstream-cost from decider mistakes. The 'Sonnet-decider mistakes cost extra elsewhere' counter-side hasn't been instrumented yet; that's a separate Phase 3 question and out of scope here.
closure_note: PROP-104/phase-0-measurement-shipped 2026-06-17. Decider STEP_MARKER breadcrumbs + compute-decider-step-cost.js shipped; operator approved Phase 0 explicitly. Phase 1/2 ship is gated on Phase 0 evidence and is the proper scope of a NEXT directive, not a continuation of this one.
